(frog-split)=
# frog-split

<!-- Generated by generate_readme.py from the CLI definitions in src/frogchem/cli. Do not edit by hand. -->

{bdg-success}`Geometry` Split a multi-XYZ file into one folder per structure, or merge several files into one.

## What it does

Conformer searches give one big file with many structures, but quantum-chemistry programs need one
input per structure. This command splits a multi-structure XYZ into one folder per conformer
(`conf_1/geom.xyz`, `conf_2/geom.xyz`, ...) — the layout the FROG ensemble tools understand, so
that later results are matched to the right conformer. With `--merge` it does the reverse:
collects single structures (e.g. the optimised geometries of each conformer) into one file to view
them together or to feed them to another command.

## How it works

```{include} _parts/frog-split/how_it_works.md
```

## Input

* **Split**: a multi-structure `.xyz` (e.g. `crest_conformers.xyz`, an MD or scan trajectory).
  ORCA/Gaussian outputs are accepted but give only their **final** geometry (one folder), not every
  optimisation step.
* **Merge**: several files (`.xyz`, ORCA or Gaussian outputs); all their structures are
  concatenated in the order you give the files. Structures taken from an ORCA/Gaussian output get
  the file name as comment line.

### Arguments

**Positional arguments**

| Argument | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `file` … | required | Input XYZ, ORCA or Gaussian file(s) |

**Options**

| Argument | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--merge` |  | Merge all inputs into a single multi-XYZ file |

**Output**

| Argument | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `-o`, `--output` `PATH` |  | Split: destination folder, <stem>_split next to the input if omitted; merge: output file, merged.xyz if omitted |
| `--out-dir` `DIR` |  | Directory for per-input output files (default: next to each input file) |
| `-f`, `--force` |  | Overwrite existing conf_<n> folders or merged file |

Shared by every command: `-v/--verbose`, `-q/--quiet` — see [CLI conventions](conventions.md).

## Output

| Kind | Name | When | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| File | `<stem>_split/conf_<n>/geom.xyz` | always | One structure per folder, n = 1, 2, ... (next to the input; -o DIR sets the folder) |
| File | `merged.xyz` | `--merge` | All structures of all inputs, comment lines kept (-o sets the path) |

### How to read it

No table, only files and messages. Example: `frog-split ensemble.xyz` on an 18-structure file
created `ensemble_split/conf_1` ... `conf_18`, each with a `geom.xyz` of 168 atoms whose comment
line is the original one (here the CREST energy, `-257.40634594`). Running it a second time printed
*"Skipped 18 existing conf_<n> folders ... (use -f to overwrite)"* and changed nothing.

* Numbering starts at **1** (`conf_1` is the first structure of the file), unlike atom indices,
  which are 0-based. CREST sorts its output by energy, so `conf_1` is the lowest CREST conformer.
* The shell sorts `conf_*` alphabetically (`conf_1, conf_10, conf_11, ..., conf_2`): with `--merge`
  the merged order follows that order, not the numeric one. List the files explicitly if order
  matters.
* With several inputs in split mode drop `-o`: each input goes to its own `<stem>_split` folder.

## Step by step

1. Split: `frog-split crest_conformers.xyz` writes `crest_conformers_split/conf_1/geom.xyz`, `conf_2/geom.xyz`, ... next to the input; use `-o structures` to choose the folder.
2. Build your calculation inputs inside each `conf_<n>` folder (keep the folder names: the conformer number is read from them by the ensemble commands).
3. Re-running on the same folder skips existing `conf_<n>` folders; add `-f` to overwrite them.
4. Merge: `frog-split --merge conf_*/geom.xyz -o ensemble.xyz` (without `-o` the result is `merged.xyz`; an existing output is overwritten only with `-f`).

## Full reference

Every option, as printed by `frog-split --help`:

:::{dropdown} `frog-split --help`
```text
usage: frog-split [-h] [-v] [-q] [--merge] [-o PATH] [--out-dir DIR] [-f] file [file ...]

Split a multi-XYZ file into one folder per structure, or merge several files into one.

Split mode writes '<dir>/conf_<n>/geom.xyz' with n starting from 1 in file order; the original
comment line of each structure is kept ('conf_<n>' when it is empty). Existing conf_<n> folders
are skipped unless -f is given. With --merge, all structures of all inputs are concatenated into
one multi-XYZ file.

positional arguments:
  file                    Input XYZ, ORCA or Gaussian file(s)

options:
  -h, --help              show this help message and exit
  --merge                 Merge all inputs into a single multi-XYZ file

output:
  -v, --verbose           Enable debug output
  -q, --quiet             Suppress banner, info and saved-file messages
  -o PATH, --output PATH  Split: destination folder, <stem>_split next to the input if omitted;
                          merge: output file, merged.xyz if omitted
  --out-dir DIR           Directory for per-input output files (default: next to each input file)
  -f, --force             Overwrite existing conf_<n> folders or merged file

outputs:
  files (next to each input, or --out-dir):
    <stem>_split/conf_<n>/geom.xyz
                                One structure per folder, n = 1, 2, ... (next to the input; -o DIR
                                sets the folder)
    merged.xyz                  [--merge] All structures of all inputs, comment lines kept (-o
                                sets the path)

examples:
  frog-split crest_conformers.xyz
      Write crest_conformers_split/conf_1/geom.xyz, conf_2/, ...
  frog-split crest_conformers.xyz -o structures -f
      Split into ./structures, overwriting
  frog-split --merge conf_*/geom.xyz -o ensemble.xyz
      Merge single structures into one ensemble

Data go to stdout, messages to stderr. Atom indices are 0-based unless stated otherwise.
Step-by-step guide (what it is for, what you need, what to expect): docs/cli/frog-split.md.
```
:::
